{{Short description|Hungarian mathematician (1927–1977)}}
{{see also|Géza Fodor (philosopher)}}{{More cn|date=August 2024}}[[File:Géza Fodor (1927-1977) Hungarian mathematician.jpg|thumb|Géza Fodor]]
'''Géza Fodor''' (6 May 1927 in [[Szeged]] &ndash; 28 September 1977 in Szeged){{Cn|date=August 2024}} was a [[Hungarian people|Hungarian]] [[mathematician]], working in [[set theory]]. He received a PhD from the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] in 1954, advised by [[László Kalmár]] and [[Paul Erdős]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Géza Fodor - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=180882 |access-date=2024-08-02 |website=www.mathgenealogy.org}}</ref> His dissertation was titled " Investigation of the structure of set mappings".<ref name=":0" />

He proved [[Fodor's lemma]] on [[stationary set]]s, one of the most important, and most used results in [[set theory]].{{Cn|date=August 2024}} He was a professor at the [[Bolyai Institute of Mathematics]] at the [[Szeged University]].{{Cn|date=August 2024}} He was vice-president, then president of the [[University of Szeged|Szeged University]]. He was elected a corresponding member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]].{{Cn|date=August 2024}}
